correctness.rationale: Every endomorphism is uniquely determined by a,c,beta mod p and d mod p^b, with phi(x)=a x+p^(b-1)c y and phi(y)=beta x+d y; it is invertible iff a and d mod p are units. Pointwise fixing A[p] forces a=1,c=0,d=1 mod p. For delta=d-1 nonzero of valuation r in [1,b-1], the v-coordinate fixed kernel has p^r elements, all divisible by p; the fixed subgroup equals A[p] iff r=1. This contributes p(p-1)p^(b-2)=(p-1)p^(b-1). The delta=0, beta nonzero case contributes p-1 exactly at b=2, while beta=0 fixes too much. Cases exhaust all possibilities including p=2. Independent exhaustive enumeration checked p,b=(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,2),(3,3),(5,2), with counts 3,4,8,8,18,24. The valuation proof establishes the universal result.

value.rationale: A[p] is the unique canonical maximal elementary-p-torsion subgroup, so counting automorphisms with exactly that fixed subgroup is a natural refinement of the established theta(A,p^2) invariant. The exact all-prime, all-b formula with exceptional b=2 provides a type-sensitive statistic that cardinality-only tables do not determine. The proof is elementary and scope narrow; the substantive motivation is the fixed-subgroup-type distinction, not computational difficulty.
